"""Greedy word wrapping.

``wrap_text`` is declared but not implemented; implementing it is one of the
bundled benchmark tasks.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> list[str]:
    """Wrap ``text`` into lines of at most ``width`` characters.

    Args:
        text: Input text. Runs of whitespace separate words.
        width: Maximum line length. Must be at least 1.

    Returns:
        The wrapped lines, without trailing whitespace. Empty input yields an
        empty list.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``width`` is less than 1.
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width must be at least 1")

    # ``str.split`` with no arguments breaks on runs of any whitespace and drops
    # leading/trailing whitespace, so each whitespace run becomes a single
    # separator (see ``wrap_text("a   b", 10) == ["a b"]``).
    words = text.split()
    if not words:
        return []

    lines: list[str] = []
    current_line = ""
    for word in words:
        # A word longer than the line budget cannot fit, so hard-split it into
        # pieces of ``width`` characters, each on its own line.
        if len(word) > width:
            for start in range(0, len(word), width):
                lines.append(word[start:start + width])
            current_line = ""
            continue

        if not current_line:
            current_line = word
        elif len(current_line) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
            # Next word still fits, so pack it onto the current line.
            current_line += " " + word
        else:
            lines.append(current_line)
            current_line = word

    if current_line:
        lines.append(current_line)

    return lines
